metadata.description: American 19th Century cluster — Civil War figures, frontier era, abolitionists, writers, and key media works. Fills gaps in American historical fiction coverage.

figures.name: Robert E. Lee
figures.title: General of the Confederate States Army
figures.description: Commander of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia whose tactical brilliance at Chancellorsville and Second Bull Run was ultimately overcome by Union resources and strategy

figures.name: Stonewall Jackson
figures.title: Confederate general
figures.description: Brilliant Confederate commander known for his Valley Campaign and stand at First Bull Run, accidentally killed by friendly fire at Chancellorsville

figures.name: John Brown
figures.title: Abolitionist
figures.description: Radical abolitionist whose raid on Harpers Ferry in 1859 electrified the nation and helped precipitate the Civil War, executed for treason

figures.name: Sojourner Truth
figures.title: Abolitionist and women's rights activist
figures.description: Born into slavery in New York, escaped to freedom and became one of the most powerful voices for abolition and women's rights, famous for her 'Ain't I a Woman?' speech

figures.name: John Wilkes Booth
figures.title: Actor and assassin
figures.description: Prominent stage actor and Confederate sympathizer who assassinated President Abraham Lincoln at Ford's Theatre on April 14, 1865

figures.name: Clara Barton
figures.title: Nurse and founder of the American Red Cross
figures.description: Civil War nurse known as the 'Angel of the Battlefield' who later founded the American Red Cross and led it for 23 years

figures.name: Sitting Bull
figures.title: Hunkpapa Lakota chief
figures.description: Lakota holy man who united the Sioux tribes against US expansion, led the coalition that defeated Custer at Little Bighorn, and became a symbol of Indigenous resistance

figures.name: Geronimo
figures.title: Apache leader
figures.description: Bedonkohe Apache leader who fought against Mexico and the United States for decades in defense of Apache lands, becoming the last Native American leader to formally surrender

figures.name: Crazy Horse
figures.title: Oglala Lakota war leader
figures.description: Visionary Lakota war leader who played a key role in the victory at Little Bighorn and resisted reservation life, killed while in custody at Fort Robinson

figures.name: Mark Twain
figures.title: American author and humorist
figures.description: Author of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, widely regarded as the father of American literature

figures.name: Walt Whitman
figures.title: American poet
figures.description: Revolutionary poet whose Leaves of Grass broke with conventional verse forms, served as a volunteer nurse during the Civil War

figures.name: Edgar Allan Poe
figures.title: American writer and critic
figures.description: Master of macabre fiction and poetry, pioneer of the detective story and a key figure in American Romanticism, died under mysterious circumstances at age 40

figures.name: Sacagawea
figures.title: Lemhi Shoshone interpreter and guide
figures.description: Shoshone woman who accompanied the Lewis and Clark Expedition as interpreter and guide, carrying her infant son across the continent to the Pacific

figures.name: Meriwether Lewis
figures.title: Explorer and governor
figures.description: Co-leader of the Corps of Discovery expedition that explored the Louisiana Purchase territory and the Pacific Northwest, later Governor of Louisiana Territory

figures.name: William Clark
figures.title: Explorer and territorial governor
figures.description: Co-leader of the Lewis and Clark Expedition, skilled cartographer who mapped the American West, later served as Superintendent of Indian Affairs

figures.name: Wyatt Earp
figures.title: Lawman and gambler
figures.description: Deputy marshal of Tombstone, Arizona, who with his brothers and Doc Holliday fought the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, becoming an enduring icon of the American West

figures.name: Billy the Kid
figures.title: Outlaw and gunfighter
figures.description: Legendary outlaw of the American Southwest who participated in the Lincoln County War and became one of the most famous figures of the Wild West

figures.name: Jesse James
figures.title: Outlaw and gang leader
figures.description: Confederate guerrilla turned bank and train robber who became a folk hero, assassinated by a member of his own gang for reward money

figures.name: Theodore Roosevelt
figures.title: 26th President of the United States
figures.description: Youngest president in US history, trust-buster, conservationist, Nobel Peace Prize winner, and leader of the Rough Riders in the Spanish-American War

figures.name: Susan B. Anthony
figures.title: Women's rights activist
figures.description: Leading figure in the women's suffrage movement who co-founded the National Woman Suffrage Association and was arrested for voting illegally in 1872

figures.name: Andrew Jackson
figures.title: 7th President of the United States
figures.description: Military hero of the Battle of New Orleans who became a populist president, championing the common man while controversially enacting the Indian Removal Act

works.title: Tombstone
works.creator: George P. Cosmatos
works.description: Western depicting Wyatt Earp's arrival in Tombstone, the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, and the Earp Vendetta Ride, with Val Kilmer's iconic portrayal of Doc Holliday

works.title: Dances with Wolves
works.creator: Kevin Costner
works.description: Epic Western about a Union soldier who befriends a band of Lakota Sioux during the Civil War era, winner of seven Academy Awards including Best Picture

works.title: Django Unchained
works.creator: Quentin Tarantino
works.description: Revisionist Western about a freed slave who teams up with a German bounty hunter to rescue his wife from a Mississippi plantation owner

works.title: Gangs of New York
works.creator: Martin Scorsese
works.description: Epic crime drama set in the Five Points neighborhood during the Civil War draft riots, depicting the clash between immigrant Irish gangs and native-born Americans

works.title: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
works.creator: Andrew Dominik
works.description: Elegiac Western depicting the final months of Jesse James's life and his betrayal by a young gang member obsessed with fame

works.title: Cold Mountain
works.creator: Anthony Minghella
works.description: Civil War drama following a wounded Confederate soldier's perilous journey home to the woman he loves in the mountains of North Carolina

works.title: The Revenant
works.creator: Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu
works.description: Survival epic based on frontier legend Hugh Glass, who was mauled by a bear and left for dead by his companions, then crawled 200 miles seeking revenge

works.title: Harriet
works.creator: Kasi Lemmons
works.description: Biographical film following Harriet Tubman's escape from slavery and her transformation into one of the most important conductors of the Underground Railroad

works.title: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
works.creator: Dee Brown
works.description: Landmark non-fiction account of the systematic destruction of Native American peoples and culture from 1860 to 1890, told from the Indigenous perspective

works.title: Gone with the Wind (novel)
works.creator: Margaret Mitchell
works.description: Pulitzer Prize-winning novel set during the Civil War and Reconstruction, following the indomitable Scarlett O'Hara through the destruction of the plantation South

works.title: Gone with the Wind (film)
works.creator: Victor Fleming
works.description: Epic romantic drama set during the Civil War, one of the highest-grossing films in cinema history, winner of ten Academy Awards

works.title: Little Women
works.creator: Louisa May Alcott
works.description: Beloved semi-autobiographical novel about four sisters growing up during the Civil War, a foundational work of American young adult literature
